Based on the search results, the **world's largest desalination plant** is located in **Saudi Arabia**.

Specifically, it is the **Ras Al-Khair Power and Desalination Plant**, situated on the eastern coast of Saudi Arabia. Key facts about this plant include:

- **Capacity**: Produces approximately 3 million cubic meters of fresh water daily (some sources cite up to 1,400,000-1,500,000 m³/day for the desalination portion alone)
- **Commissioned**: April 2014 (full commercial operation by March 2016)
- **Power generation**: 2,400 MW (combined cycle gas turbines)
- **Hybrid technology**: Uses a combination of multi-stage flashing (thermal) and reverse osmosis systems
- **Operator**: Saline Water Conversion Corporation of Saudi Arabia

The plant has been recognized by Guinness World Records and won the 2015 Global Water Awards "Desalination Plant of the Year" award. It supplies both electricity and freshwater to major cities including Riyadh and Hafr Al-Batin.

The **Ras Al-Khair Power and Desalination Plant** is a [power] and [desalination plant] located in [Ras Al-Khair] on the eastern coast of [Saudi Arabia]. It is operated by the [Saline Water Conversion Corporation] of Saudi Arabia. The plant began operating in April 2014 and, as of January 2017[[update]], is the world's largest hybrid water desalination plant.[[1]][[2]] The project includes a power plant capable of producing 2400 [MW] of electricity.[[1]] In 2015, it won the Global Water Awards "Desalination Plant of the Year" award.[[3]][[4]]

## History

[[edit]]

Construction of the plant began in 2011.[[5]] Though originally slated to begin producing freshwater by the end of 2013,[[6]] the first freshwater produced from the plant was in early 2015.[[7]] Full commercial operation of the plant was achieved in March 2016.[[8]]

The primary contractors for construction of the plant were the [Doosan Group] and [Saudi Archirodon]").[[5]] Doosan was awarded the prime contract in September, 2010.[[9]] Additional contractors for the plant included [Fluid Equipment Development Company] for energy recovery devices, [Siemens] for generators, turbines, and related equipment, and [Hyosung] for various motors.[[5]]

The plant has created 3,500 direct and indirect jobs.[[1]][[10]]

## Operation

[[edit]]

Water intake for the plant comes from the [Persian Gulf], on the shore of which the plant sits.[[5]] The plant includes five high-efficiency [gas turbines operated in combined cycle mode] and in single mode.[[5]] It uses a hybrid system of eight [multi-stage flashing] units and 17 [reverse osmosis] units.[[11]] Freshwater output from the plant is pumped via pipelines to [Riyadh] and [Hafr Al-Batin].[[1]] Electricity and freshwater output from the plant also supply a nearby [aluminium oxide] refinery.[[5]] Of the 2400 MW electricity produced by the plant, 200 MW are used by the plant itself.[[7]][Effluent] from the plant is processed locally by a dedicated wastewater treatment plant and discharged into the Persian Gulf.[[5]]
